question: What does Cirrus Logic do, why is our new-capital verdict REJECTED despite its $1.08B cash pile and 53% gross margins, and what is our current holding action and capital redeployment plan?

epigraph.quote: Concentration builds wealth only when you control the customer relationship; when one customer controls 93% of your revenue, concentration is a silent liability.
epigraph.author: Institutional Research Desk

web_blocks.html: **Cirrus Logic, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRUS)** is a fabless chip designer based in Austin, Texas [1]. It builds custom 22nm audio codecs, boosted amplifiers, haptic drivers, camera controllers, and PC SoundWire chips [1][2][15]. Our price-blind business audit (Chapters 1–6) assigns a **`CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL`** quality rating and **`PASS_WITH_WATCH`** KPI health. The firm owns 4,340 patents, posts 52.8%–53.7% GAAP gross margins, earns 34.7% operating ROIC, and holds $1,076.43 million in cash with zero debt [1][2]. Yet Apple concentration rose from 79% in FY2017 to **91% in FY2026** and **93% in Q2 FY2027** [1][2]. Nine-year revenue growth is just 2.9% per year, and Q3 FY2027 guidance ($510M–$570M) implies a 7% YoY drop [3].

At the November 24, 2026 close of **$115.72** (-35.86% off its $180.42 high), CRUS looks cheap at 14.61x P/E and 10.03x EV/EBITDA [27][28]. However, our ex-SBC 10-year DCF uses a $430M normalized FCF base (stripping FY2026's ~$102M working-capital boost and deducting $81.81M SBC at 10.8% WACC). That puts Base fair value at **$126.00** (+8.9%) and probability-weighted value at **$124.25** (+7.4%). With a structural stop at **$104.50** (below the $105.10 low, 2.62x ATR), reward-to-risk is just **0.69:1** from $117.25 (**0.92:1** from CMP). Price also sits **-12.53% below its 30-week SMA ($132.30)** and **-15.91% below its 200-day SMA ($137.61)** in a Downtrend market [28][41]. Options are illiquid (**`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`**). **New Capital Verdict: `REJECTED` (`VALUATION`, `TREND`) | Current Holding Action: `NOT_HELD` (0 shares) | Redeployment: `100% USD CASH`**.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional monograph on Cirrus Logic, Inc. (NASDAQ: CRUS). Before you and I dive into forty years of semiconductor pivots, custom 22-nanometer audio silicon, and ten years of audited SEC cash-flow statements, let me put our independent conclusion squarely on the table—derived strictly after completing our price-blind business audit and weighing every valuation and technical gate.

Cirrus Logic is a classic study in financial contrast. On the surface, its operating metrics look enviable: $1.997 billion in FY2026 revenue, 52.8% to 53.7% GAAP gross margins, 34.7% operating return on invested capital, $1.08 billion in cash and marketable securities, zero funded debt, and a decade of disciplined buybacks that shrank diluted shares by more than 20%. Yet look one layer deeper and you discover why Wall Street refuses to grant Cirrus Logic an analog-leader multiple: Apple accounted for 91% of revenue in FY2026 and surged to 93% in Q2 FY2027. Nine-year revenue growth is just 2.9% annualized, the $335 million Lion Semiconductor diversification bet incurred an $85.8 million write-down, Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance dropped 7% year-over-year at the midpoint, and 2026–2027 PC memory shortages are pushing laptop audio ramps into FY2028. That is why our price-blind business verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health.

At the November 24, 2026 close of $115.72—down 35.86% from its $180.42 52-week high—CRUS trades at 14.61x trailing P/E and 10.03x EV/EBITDA. That looks cheap until you strip out FY2026's one-time $102 million working-capital cash release and treat $81.81 million of annual stock-based compensation as a real economic cost. On a normalized $430 million ex-SBC free cash flow baseline and a 10.8% WACC (anchored by a 4.92% 10-year Treasury yield), our Base intrinsic value is $126.00 per share (+8.9%), our Bull case is $160.50 (+38.7%), and our Bear case is $84.50 (-27.0%). Probability-weighted expected return is just +7.4%—below our 10.8% hurdle rate—and reward-to-risk against a realistic $104.50 structural stop is a sub-1:1 ratio of 0.69:1 to 0.92:1.

The chart confirms the valuation caution. CRUS sits 12.53% below its 30-week moving average ($132.30) and 15.91% below its 200-day moving average ($137.61) inside a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend where just 2.0% of semiconductor stocks trade above their 50-day EMA. Listed options carry spreads wider than 14% (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID). Because we hold zero shares (NOT_HELD) and our consolidated U.S. portfolio holds only 8.73% cash against 225.3% beta-weighted market exposure, our verdict is an unambiguous REJECTED on Valuation and Trend, keeping 100% of marginal capital in USD cash while deferring both Stage 2 shortlist ETF XLV (0%) and analog peer SLAB (0%). Let us now trace the full evidence chapter by chapter.

book_callouts.title: How to Read This Monograph
book_callouts.text: Chapters 1 through 6 were written strictly price-blind—without looking at CRUS's share price, valuation multiple, or chart—so that business reality could never be bent to justify a cheap P/E. Chapters 7 through 9 then confront that locked business audit with today's $115.72 price, analog peer multiples, multi-timeframe technicals, and our live U.S. portfolio constraints.
